issue: The annotation 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' points to the green backfill segment, not to the end of the finishing blue sequence or the freed-slot boundary.
evidence: The arrow from the annotation terminates on the narrow green bar in the top row. The finishing sequence is the blue bar immediately to its left; the green bar is the new sequence that fills the freed slot.
acceptance_test: Redirect the arrow to the boundary between the finishing blue sequence and the green backfill, or reword the annotation to 'a freed slot is refilled immediately' and keep the arrow on the green segment. Verify the annotation's subject and arrow target agree.

issue: In the rendered page, all four blue 'sequence in flight' segments appear to terminate at the same x-position, with the pink idle region beginning at that same x in every row. If the blues are uniform, no sequence finishes early, the batch's 'slowest member' is all four simultaneously, and the depicted trailing idle has no cause — contradicting the figure's own labels.
evidence: Caption: 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in the trailing slots'. In-figure label: 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. Both require visibly different sequence lengths; the slowest row should show no (or negligible) pink. Rendered inspection at 150 dpi shows four equal-width blues and four pink regions starting at the same x; the 'idle (bubble)' arrow points into row 3's pink as if it were early-finish idle. Confidence is limited by render resolution — this must be checked against the figure source.
root_cause: Either the drawn row lengths are actually equal (semantic error: idle depicted without differential finish times), or differences are too small to read at print size (visual error: the mechanism is invisible).
correction: Make the four blue segments end at clearly different x-positions, with the longest (slowest) row's blue extending to the batch end and little or no pink, so the pink width per row visibly equals that row's early-finish margin.
acceptance_test: At print size, a reader can see at least three distinct blue-end positions; the slowest row shows no pink; pink width per row is proportional to how much earlier that sequence finished; the 'finishes early' label points at a row that is visibly shorter than the slowest row.

issue: The legend defines green as 'new sequence (backfill)', but the right panel draws green as thin vertical bars between blue segments; the new sequence then continues as blue. This makes green look like an instantaneous admission marker, not a sequence with duration.
evidence: Legend: 'new sequence (backfill)' = green. Right panel: each row shows blue bar → narrow green vertical bar → blue bar. Caption: 'new sequences (green) snap into free slots' and 'freed slots are refilled every step.' A sequence occupying a slot should have duration; the drawn green segment is one step wide and is followed by blue.
acceptance_test: Either redraw the green backfill as a block spanning the new sequence's decode steps (with the legend unchanged), or relabel green as 'admission event' and use a distinct color/pattern for the new sequence's in-flight duration. Verify that a reader can identify which sequence occupies the slot after backfill without reading the caption.

issue: The discrete-batching panel draws four sequences of IDENTICAL length (four equal blue blocks, four equal pink trailing regions). The mechanism the caption and the figure's own annotation describe — 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in trailing slots' and 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early' — requires at least one visibly shorter sequence. As drawn, the picture is equally consistent with the opposite reading: all four sequences ended together and the slots sat idle until the next batch was admitted. The reader therefore cannot see the phenomenon the figure exists to contrast with continuous batching.
evidence: Rendered left panel: four rows, each with an identical short blue block at the left and an identical long pink dotted region to the right, all ending at the same x. Caption: 'In the left (discrete) panel a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in trailing slots'. In-figure annotation: 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. Neither is visible in the drawing.
acceptance_test: In the discrete panel, at least one sequence must be drawn visibly shorter than the others, with that row's pink idle region extending past the other rows' blue regions, so that 'short outputs idle in trailing slots' and 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early' are both readable from the drawing alone. Confirm at print size that the length difference is unambiguous.

issue: Grayscale failure with information loss. 'sequence in flight' is encoded as a solid blue block and 'new sequence (backfill)' as a solid green block — hue is the ONLY distinguishing channel. In grayscale the backfill strips are indistinguishable from in-flight blocks, and the figure's entire point (a slot being refilled by a new sequence) disappears. Unlike FIGURE 10.1, this figure's blocks carry no text labels, so there is no redundant channel to fall back on. The legend swatches are also solid color only.
evidence: Rendered legend: 'idle slot (bubble)' = pink dotted swatch; 'sequence in flight' = solid blue swatch; 'new sequence (backfill)' = solid green swatch. The only texture difference in the panels is the dotted pink idle region; blue and green are both solid fills.
acceptance_test: Render the figure in grayscale and confirm the backfill strip remains distinguishable from an in-flight block by texture or outline (e.g. hatched or outlined green), not hue alone; the legend swatches must reproduce the same texture used in the panels.

issue: The legend row ('idle slot (bubble) | sequence in flight | new sequence (backfill)') is set noticeably smaller than the panel titles 'Discrete batching' / 'Continuous batching' and smaller than the in-panel annotations. The legend is the only key to the figure's three encodings, so it is the last element that should be shrunk; if it falls below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor, the color/pattern key becomes hard to read at print size.
evidence: Rendered page: legend glyph height is visibly below that of the bold panel titles and below the 'idle (bubble)' / 'new sequences (green) snap into freed slots' annotations.
acceptance_test: Measure the legend text at print size: it must be at or above the 8 pt figure-annotation floor and must not be smaller than the panel titles or the in-panel annotations. Confirm by rendering the page at 100% and reading the legend without magnification.

issue: A single horizontal arrow labeled 'time (decode steps / iterations) ->' spans the full width of the figure, running under both the discrete and the continuous panels. The two panels are separate illustrations on unrelated scales (the discrete panel's rows all start at the same x; the continuous panel's rows are staggered diagonally), so one shared axis implies a common timeline and a common scale that does not exist. The reader may also read the diagonal stagger in the right panel as a time axis, which the figure never states.
evidence: Rendered figure: one arrow from the left edge under the discrete panel to the right edge under the continuous panel; the caption separately says 'The horizontal axis is time (decode steps / iterations)' without restricting it to one panel.
acceptance_test: Either draw the time axis under each panel separately, or state in the caption and in the figure that the two panels are independent illustrations not on a common scale. If the diagonal stagger in the continuous panel encodes time, label it; if not, align the rows so no unintended diagonal reading is possible.

issue: The in-figure note reads 'Decode-only illustration: every request is in the prefill->decode phase.' The phrase 'in the prefill->decode phase' is ambiguous and reads as though requests are in the prefill phase or the decode phase, which contradicts the 'Decode-only' label immediately preceding it. The intended statement is that the requests shown are in the decode phase only.
evidence: Rendered note under the time axis: 'Decode-only illustration: every request is in the prefill->decode phase. A real system also interleaves prefill of new requests into the same steps (§11.4, Ch 15).'
acceptance_test: The note must read 'every request shown is in the decode phase' (or equivalent) so that it cannot be read as including the prefill phase, and must remain consistent with the caption's 'The diagram is a decode-only illustration'.

issue: The table title 'Table 11-1 — Serving techniques at a glance' is the last line of the page, stranded at the page bottom with the table body presumably starting on PDF 208 — an orphaned table caption.
evidence: Rendered page 187 ends with the italic table title and blank space below it; no header row or data rows follow on this page.
root_cause: Table float/caption break not kept with the table body.
correction: Keep the title with at least the table header (ideally the first rows) on the same page.
acceptance_test: No table caption in the book appears as the final content line of a page while its table body begins on the next page; specifically, Table 11-1's title and header row share a page.

issue: The caption 'Table 11-1 — Serving techniques at a glance' is stranded at the bottom of the page with no table content; the table begins on the following page.
evidence: At the bottom of printed p.187 the italic caption appears alone; no table header or rows follow on the page. The table is therefore separated from its caption.
acceptance_test: Keep the caption with the table header on the same page (move the caption to the table's page or move the table start to p.187); verify no orphaned table caption remains.

issue: Box 4 uses a dashed border while boxes 1–3 use solid borders; the distinction is never explained in the figure or caption, yet a dashed border is the only non-color difference among the four boxes.
evidence: Caption says the four are 'independent dials' and that 'the canonical baseline uses the first three; resource specialization joins when the workload outgrrows a node (see "When to Disaggregate", §11.3)' — a plausible intent for the dashed border (not in the baseline), but the encoding is unstated, so a reader may read the dashed border as 'weaker', 'optional', or 'different category'.
root_cause: Visual semantics used without a legend or caption sentence.
correction: Either make all four borders consistent, or state the dashed border's meaning in the caption or an in-figure note (e.g., 'dashed = not in the canonical baseline; joins at scale').
acceptance_test: Every border-style variation in the book's figures is either explained where it appears or eliminated; a grayscale reader can account for the dashed border from text alone.

issue: Grayscale distinguishability: boxes 1, 2 and 3 are separated only by border hue (purple, red, green), all solid; only box 4's dashed orange border survives a grayscale conversion. The figure's central claim is that the four concerns are separable and independently chosen, and the dashed-vs-solid contrast is doing real work for box 4 alone. The 'e.g.' sub-labels are also hue-matched, so in grayscale the sub-label loses its association with its box border. The bold box titles keep the content readable, so this is a polish-and-robustness issue rather than information loss.
evidence: Rendered figure: box 1 purple solid border with purple italic 'e.g. continuous batching'; box 2 red solid with red italic 'e.g. PagedAttention (KV pages)'; box 3 green solid with green italic 'e.g. prefix caching'; box 4 orange DASHED with orange italic 'e.g. P/D disaggregation'.
acceptance_test: Render in grayscale and confirm all four boxes remain distinguishable by border style (e.g. solid / dashed / double / corner marker) rather than hue alone, and that the dashed border remains reserved for box 4 so the caption's 'the canonical baseline uses the first three; resource specialization joins when the workload outgrows a node' is still visually legible.

issue: The page opens with roughly 1.5-2 inches of completely blank space between the running head and the figure title, and the figure-plus-caption block then floats in the upper-middle of the page with a large blank band below. The page contains no body text, so the leading void reads as an accidental float placement rather than a designed plate.
evidence: Rendered PDF 211 / printed 191: running head at the top, then blank space until the figure title 'Serving = four separable concerns, not a stack', then the four boxes, then the caption, then blank space to the foot of the page.
acceptance_test: Top-align the figure block with the text block (or reduce the leading whitespace) so the page does not open with an empty band; confirm in the final PDF that no page in the chapter carries a comparable unexplained leading void.
